= 69091C | socks3 = 69091C }} '''Aston Villa Football Club''' is a professional [[Association football|football]] club based in [[Aston]], [[Birmingham]], England. Founded in 1874, it competes in the [[Premier League]], the top tier of [[English football league system|English football]], and has played at its home ground, [[Villa Park]], since 1897. Aston Villa is one of the oldest and most successful clubs in England, having won the [[Football League First Division]] seven times, the [[FA Cup]] seven times, the [[EFL Cup|League Cup]] five times, as well as the [[European Cup]], [[UEFA Super Cup|European Super Cup]], and [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] once. During the 1880s, Aston Villa were a pioneer of the modern [[passing game]], introduced by Scotsman [[George Ramsay (footballer, born 1855)|George Ramsay]], who Villa appointed as the world's first professional football [[Manager (association football)|manager]] in 1886. The club was influential in the sport's move to [[Professionalism in association football|professionalism]] in 1885, and it was a Villa director, [[William McGregor (football)|William McGregor]], who founded the world's first [[1888–89 Football League|Football League in 1888]]. Ramsay's trophy haul of six League Championships and six FA Cups established Aston Villa as the most successful club in England, a position it held from the 1890s until the 1970s. Villa scored a record 128 goals in [[1930–31 Aston Villa F.C. season|1930–31]], however the club began its first decline in the mid-1930s; the 1940s and 1950s were generally a period of mediocrity followed by a steep decline in the 1960s which culminated in a takeover of the club by [[Doug Ellis]] in 1968 and Villa's first and only [[Promotion and relegation|relegation]] to the third tier of English football in [[1969–70 Aston Villa F.C. season|1969–70]]. Villa returned to the top tier from the mid-1970s under manager [[Ron Saunders]], who led the club to a seventh top-flight league title in [[1980–81 Aston Villa F.C. season|1980–81]]. They became only the fourth English club to win the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]], in [[1981–82 European Cup|1981–82]], followed by victory in the [[1982 European Super Cup]]. In [[1992–93 Aston Villa F.C. season|1992]], Aston Villa were founding members of the [[Premier League]], one of only three sides to have been a founding member of both the Football League and the Premier League. Throughout the 1990s and early 2000s, Villa regularly qualified for European football, but following a period of decline after the departure of [[Martin O'Neill]] the club suffered its only relegation from the Premier League in [[2015–16 Aston Villa F.C. season|2015–16]]. After three seasons in the [[EFL Championship]] and two ownership changes, the club returned to the Premier League in [[2018–19 Aston Villa F.C. season|2019]]. Under [[Unai Emery]], the club qualified for the [[UEFA Champions League]] for the first time since [[1982–83 Aston Villa F.C. season|1982–83]] and won the [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] in [[2025–26 UEFA Europa League|2025–26]]. During its history, Villa has spent 113 seasons in the top-flight, the second highest of any club, and has provided 78 [[England Internationals|England internationals]], also the second highest of any club. Aston Villa is ranked fifth in the all-time English top flight table since its creation in 1888,{{cite web |title=Premier League + 1. Division – All-time league table |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/competition/co91/records-all-time-table/ |access-date=12 March 2025 |website=worldfootball.net |date=12 March 2025 |archive-date=10 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251210023031/https://www.worldfootball.net/competition/co91/records-all-time-table/ |url-status=live }} and is the [[List of football clubs in England by competitive honours won|seventh most successful club]] in English football by competitive honours. Villa have a fierce local rivalry with [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] and the [[Second City derby]] between the teams has been played [[1879–80 Aston Villa F.C. season|since 1879]]. There is also a local rivalry with [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]], with matches between the sides known as the [[Aston Villa F.C.–West Bromwich Albion F.C. rivalry|West Midlands derby]]. The club's traditional [[Kit (association football)|kit]] colours are [[Wine (color)#Claret|claret]] shirts with sky blue sleeves, white shorts and sky blue socks, and its traditional club badge features a [[Attitude (heraldry)#Rampant|rampant]] lion. The club has been fully owned by [[V Sports]] since 2019."}}
